title: try & except: Building Safety Nets 🥅
description: Catch exceptions before they crash your script – graceful degradation for real‑world hacking tools.

slides.title: The Problem with Crashes
slides.content:
# A Single Error Stops Everything

If your port scanner crashes on port 100 out of 1000, you lose all previous results. Hacking tools must be resilient.

`try`/`except` lets you say: "Try this risky code. If it fails, do this instead – don't crash."

slides.title: Basic try/except

quizData.question: A bare `except:` catches every possible exception, including system exits.
quizData.explanation: Yes, it catches everything – which can hide serious bugs. Usually avoid it.

slides.title: Catch Specific Exceptions
slides.content:
# Be Precise: `except ValueError:`

```python
try:
    port = int(user_input)
except ValueError:
    print("Port must be a number")
```
* Only catches `ValueError`; other errors still crash (so you notice them).
* You can handle multiple different types with multiple `except` blocks.

slides.title: Multiple except Clauses

quizData.question: Why is `except Exception:` better than bare `except:`?

options.text: It doesn't catch KeyboardInterrupt or SystemExit

quizData.explanation: Bare except catches system‑level exceptions that should usually propagate; `except Exception` is safer.

slides.title: Catching Multiple Types in One Block
slides.content:
# Use a Tuple

```python
try:
    risky_code()
except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
    print(f"Input error: {e}")
```
The `as e` captures the exception object – you can print it or log it.

slides.title: Accessing the Exception Object

quizData.question: What does `except (A, B) as e:` do?

options.text: Catches A or B, and binds the exception to e
Catches both A and B simultaneously

quizData.explanation: It catches any of the listed exception types and assigns the instance to e.

slides.title: Where to Place try/except
slides.content:
# Wrap the Smallest Risky Block

Don't wrap your whole script in one giant try block – it makes debugging hard.

Good:
```python
for host in hosts:
    try:
        scan(host)
    except ConnectionError:
        print(f"{host} unreachable, skipping")
```
This way, one failed host doesn't stop the entire scan.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Log Exceptions, Don't Hide Them

```python
import traceback
try:
    dangerous()
except Exception:
    traceback.print_exc()   # prints full traceback without crashing
```
This is excellent for logging while continuing execution.
